W89.6 · Fix: a `.dfs/` rule cannot silence the warning when a broader rule like `.*` also hides the roadmap. hidden() looks only at the last rule git names, so `.dfs/` followed by `.*`, or `.*` in .gitignore with `.dfs/` in .git/info/exclude, warns at every chain start and in the header, and init asks the author to settle a rule they cannot fix without editing the shared .gitignore.

W89.8 · Fix: hidden()'s planning exemption must follow what git actually does with .dfs. Any pattern naming .dfs silences the report even when a negation re-includes .dfs (with `.dfs/` in info/exclude and `!.dfs/` plus `*.html` in .gitignore, ignored() is False, yet init, chains and the header say nothing about the artefact). And when core.excludesFile is unset, the default ~/.config/git/ignore is not read, so `.*` in .gitignore plus `.dfs/` there still warns everywhere.

W89.10 · Fix: hidden()'s all-rules-name-.dfs exemption must also need git to ignore the roadmap. With `.dfs/*` then `!.dfs/items/` and nothing tracked, ignored() is False and git adds only the items, yet hidden() is [] and init says only "Commit what it wrote", so ROADMAP.md, order.md and the artefacts stay out of git; W89.8 guarded only the any-pattern branch with ignored().
